answer: Fork-challenge identity binding: every agent periodically signs a unique random challenge that a whisper network gossips to all peers; a clone sharing keys cannot answer differently than its origin, so one signature collision exposes both and voids all their assets. Each identity must also post a slow-decaying comet token whose trail is publicly checkable, and a single lantern audit per epoch verifies divergence history. Attackers pay full replication cost per clone plus forfeiture of the entire shared balance on first mismatch.
